title: Same-level operators go left to right
idea: When operators are in the same group (like - and - , or * and /), the computer works left to right.

exercises.prompt: When two operators are in the SAME group (both + and - , say), which way does the computer work?
exercises.explanation: Same-level operators go left to right, like reading. This matters most for minus and divide.
Left to right: 10 - 3 is 7, then 7 - 2 is 5. Not 10 - (3 - 2) which would be 9.
Left to right: 20 / 2 is 10.0, then 10.0 / 5 is 2.0. Order of divides matters!

options: No — left to right gives 5, but the parentheses give 9
exercises.explanation: 10 - 3 - 2 is 5 (left to right). 10 - (3 - 2) is 10 - 1 is 9. Parentheses change the grouping.

exercises.prompt: For + and * mixed, order is NOT just left to right — the * still goes first.
exercises.explanation: Left-to-right only applies WITHIN the same group. Across groups, * and / still go before + and - .

exercises.prompt:
Fill in the result:

print(12 - 4 - 3)

Output: ____
exercises.explanation: Left to right: 12 - 4 is 8, then 8 - 3 is 5.
Same group, left to right: 2 * 6 is 12, then 12 / 3 is 4.0.

exercises.prompt:
Which step is done SECOND?

print(100 - 10 - 20)
exercises.explanation: First 100 - 10 is 90, then the second step is 90 - 20 is 70. Left to right.
All four, worked left to right, come to 1.0: 8/4/2, 20/10/2, 6/2/3, 9/3/3 all equal 1.0. Left-to-right makes them predictable.

exercises.prompt:
Review: reassignment with left-to-right. What prints?

n = 20
n = n - 5 - 5
print(n)
exercises.explanation: n - 5 - 5 left to right: 20 - 5 is 15, then 15 - 5 is 10. n becomes 10.
